rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~10 at.% V to NbMoTaW, while the paper compared equiatomic NbMoTaW with an equiatomic Re-containing NbMoTaWRe film. Both are compositional modifications of the same base alloy, but the specific added element (V vs. Re) and the amount (10 at.% vs. 20 at.%) differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions room-temperature mechanical testing, high-temperature testing up to 1600 °C, and helium ion irradiation, but the paper's experiments were conducted entirely at room temperature (deposition, irradiation, and mechanical testing) with specific 120 keV He2+ parameters. The hypothesis does not match the paper's room-temperature-only regime or its specific irradiation conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes increased lattice distortion and enhanced defect recombination to improve ductility and irradiation tolerance, while the paper's mechanism relies on additional grain boundaries, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions acting as defect sinks to suppress He-bubble growth and segregation. Both are defect-sink mechanisms, but the structural mediators (lattice distortion/precipitates vs. grain boundaries/amorphous regions) and specific pathways differ.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased room-temperature ductility, reduced irradiation damage, and maintained high-temperature strength. The paper's actual result was reduced irradiation hardening and grain-boundary embrittlement at room temperature, with no high-temperature testing. The predicted property (irradiation resistance) and direction (improvement) align, but the hypothesis adds ductility and high-temperature strength outcomes not measured in the paper.
